P1.evidence: No setter code in the title and no application referenced, so the read-back check does not apply. The same three-part frame this rep uses throughout: 'it's just about me understanding where you're at. You know, where are you today? Where do you want to be? If we can help, I can show you some options. Okay?' — missing 'what's in the way'. Agreement was the trailing 'Okay?' answered 'Yeah'. The open question was clean: 'How can we potentially help you?'

P2.evidence: By a wide margin the best Baseline in this folder, and the only call in the batch where the rep announced the block and ran it: 'Now, let's get a bit of a baseline before we continue the conversation.' Age, height and weight all obtained — 'You're 53, Paul. How tall are you?' and 'And what's your weight?' — 74kg at roughly six foot. Work covered including the desk-bound question: 'is this job, what are you going to be doing on a day-to-day basis? Are you going to be sitting down a lot?' — 'No, I'm on my feet all day.' The injury probing is genuinely good and stands out against every other call here: 'You mentioned the shoulder a couple of times now. Is that right or left?', 'What happened?', 'What happened there?' on the steroid reaction, and 'How long ago was that?' pinning the layoff at eighteen months. Diet was asked with a nice guard against assumption — 'you're a caterer, so I can imagine that's maybe taken care of, but I don't presume anything' — and energy was asked on a scale with the afternoon lull surfaced. Sleep was asked only as quality ('are you waking up rested?'), not quantity. The training week was inferred rather than elicited. The one clear miss is health conditions: no general or hereditary health question was ever asked, so what is known medically is only what he chose to raise.

P3.evidence: Strong throughout. The paintbrush was anchored to a date — 'it's May the 4th, 2026. How do you want to show up May the 4th, 2027?' — and produced an unusually mature answer: 'first and foremost, it would actually be consistency... I'm not going to sit here and say I want to be 78 kilos and 10% body fat, none of that matters.' The bridge was asked plainly — 'how do you want to show up in the world?' — and the best question on the call followed it: 'you being consistent and proving that to yourself first and foremost, how is that going to change the relationship that you have with yourself?', which produced 'I might actually smile at myself and thank myself instead of calling myself an idiot.' The who-else move ran — 'aside from yourself, who's going to benefit from this?' — reaching partner, business partner and customers, and the reflect-back closed it: 'Can you see how this is more than just swinging a few kettlebells around? What we just said there is the top of the mountain.' Only the can't-do-yet question is short: pull-ups, hanging and overhead lifting were named as limitations by the prospect, never asked as aspirations.

P4.evidence: Complete. Past attempts were named and then properly worked: Colin and Flow, the Guildford private members gym, multiple physios, gym memberships and two personal trainers. 'What happened?' pulled out the burnout, 'What happened there?' pulled out the steroid reaction, and the root-cause question was asked with an edge that landed: 'since then, I don't want to be disrespectful, but what's really been the excuse for yourself?' — answered 'There isn't one.' The rep then named the gap and had it confirmed: 'Would you say that part of the reason why the 18 months have been the way they are is due to comfort?' — 'Yeah, yeah, absolutely.' The information-isn't-the-problem move is scored partial because it was delivered as the comfort frame rather than the scripted challenge, though on a prospect with a nutrition degree who already knows what to do it arguably landed better.

P5.evidence: Well run apart from the horizon. The settle-for move was excellent and did not soften: 'a lot of people are okay in their bodies and that's fine. But I don't feel like for you, that's something you're willing to accept' — 'No, I keep coming back to it. And I've been coming back to it for too long.' The why-not was pursued twice, once through the comfort-zone question and once with 'A lot of people, and especially in the UK, are comfortable like that. I guess what makes you different?' The line in the sand was asked directly: 'So the million dollar question, are you actually ready to take [the step]?' What is missing is the explicit cost-of-inaction over a stated horizon — the rep asked how he wants to show up in a year, which is the positive image, and the prospect had to supply the negative one himself: 'what happens if you don't, well, just sit here watching films, not doing it, and then waking up thinking, well, I'm still not doing it.'

P6.evidence: The capability check was asked in near-scripted form — 'do you feel like you're internally capable of actually really getting to the body and the health that you've mentioned?' — and returned an explicit no-not-yet: 'There is a wobble there. As soon as you said that, there's the doubt pops in. I'm like, Oh, am I? Can I? Can I actually do it?' The script is unambiguous that this routes back to Phase 5. The rep instead normalised it — 'Good. It's meant to be there' — let the prospect talk himself through his own injury history, and moved to price. The all-in question was never asked. The trust gauge was run and answered well ('I do think I need it'), but a stated wobble on capability is not the clear YES the script requires before presenting.

P11.evidence: A soft close was attempted — 'Which one are you kind of gravitating towards in this meeting?' — and the prospect declined to decide, so payment, the Trevor booking, the agreement and onboarding were all unreachable. The rep booked a second call instead, confirmed the invite had arrived and been saved, and collected email and phone number.

objection_plays.detail: SCRIPT GAP AND THE CENTRAL FINDING OF THIS CALL — clinical fit, third instance in this batch. The trigger here is the strongest in the corpus: an ultrasound-confirmed bursal pathology that rules out hanging and confident overhead loading, a documented adverse drug reaction, a declined second injection, a slipped-disc history with epidurals, and a named osteopath's opinion that training does not suit him. The playbook offers nothing, so the rep improvised — and what he improvised was to dismiss the clinician: 'I'm just going to be direct with you, that's rubbish.' He then gave a partial mitigation on his own initiative ('especially for someone with the injury track record, like yourself... you're not going to be given a hard weight to start off with') and correctly told him to get an 8kg bell. The missing move is the one that does not exist anywhere in the script: pause, put the programme in front of the physiotherapist he is already seeing, and close conditionally on her sign-off. That path was available, free, and never mentioned.

A clear affordability trigger — 'given my financial situation at the moment, and knowing where my credit card's at', 'I won't be able to commit to the six or 12. I just don't have the funds for that', and unprompted disclosure that the business has been 'earning relatively just enough to cover our bills for the last kind of six months' with cash going into the fit-out. Not one move of the play ran: no isolation, no HOW-not-SHOULD frame, no permission question and none of the six financial-picture questions. Scored a miss against the script, but note the commercial judgement was probably better than the play would have produced — the rep thanked him for the honesty, explained the differential mechanic so nothing is lost by starting small, and then actively recommended the cheapest tier: 'if I was just telling you what to do, just do the one month. Don't do the three.' Compare directly with the Andrew Freeman call the same day, where the play also did not run and $9,000 was taken from a prospect with disclosed job instability.

Fear was present in two distinct forms and the rep worked both. Concrete fear of re-injury with a livelihood attached — 'I don't want to get injured again. I work for myself now, I have to go to work, I don't get sick pay' — and abstract self-doubt at the decision point: 'are you really ready for this? Can you commit to it? Are you going to do it? Or are you going to fail again?' Ran: a variant of the PLANE move using skydiving, the naming of fear as the universal blocker, 'that's probably the fear talking', 'At the precipice of making a decision like this, that voice grows louder' and the counter-voice framing. Not run: 'Would it be fair to say you're looking for certainty?', the BRIDGE, and above all BURNED BEFORE — which was written for exactly this prospect, who has been hurt by training twice and by a steroid injection once, and which was never used. The rep also closed the call by pre-empting future doubt: 'Over the next few days, that voice is going to grow louder... just remember that.'

'I need to sleep on it' and 'I just need some time to process it all.' One scripted probe ran — 'what else do you kind of need to think of before making your decision?' — and the rep then booked Wednesday. None of the deciding-not-thinking sequence was attempted. Worth noting that the prospect had pre-empted it explicitly and the rep respected the boundary: 'I wouldn't make a decision now. And I think if you tried to get me to, I'd probably say, all right, I won't do it. Then I'd probably just go.' Given that, stopping was almost certainly the right call and the partial score reflects the script rather than the judgement.

SCRIPT GAP — the prospect who has already failed with a comparable remote coach. He named the competitor, the format and the failure mode: 'I dipped into kettlebells about two and a half, three years ago, started training with another American trainer called Colin, does Flow... I just found it a little bit hard to follow. I had to keep clicking on my phone to get the videos up... everything was meant to take 30 minutes, 45 minutes. It would take me an hour, hour and 20.' Then the general form: 'I am dubious about online coaching... how do they really see what you're doing?' Third appearance of the remote-versus-in-person objection in this batch and still nothing scripted. The film-and-review loop is the answer and it was described generically rather than aimed at the objection.

SCRIPT GAP — the prospect who has tried a programme component and it harmed him. He said fasting has never suited him at any point, and separately described a previous episode of burnout with rapid unintended fat and weight loss on a five-day training week. There is no scripted path for de-scoping a pillar, so the rep overrode instead: 'especially if we're over 40, fasting directly contributes to having longevity' and 'Trevor's here to kind of correct that for yourself. We should, we have the capacity to fast.' A play that allows a rep to say 'then we won't do that part' would have cost nothing here and would have removed the only substantive objection to pillar two.

notes: Read alongside the rest of this folder, this call proves the rep can run the process — Baseline, Goals, Past Attempts and Consequence all scored hit, which happens nowhere else in the batch, and the injury probing at 00:03:53 is the best discovery sequence in the corpus. Two things to correct. First, he elicited a full injury history and then used none of it as a gate: the correct output of that Baseline was 'let's get your physio to look at the movement library before you pay me', and instead a named clinician's advice was called rubbish. Second, an explicit capability wobble at 00:52:49 was normalised rather than routed back to Phase 5, and price was presented against it four minutes later. Everything else here is good work.
